title: Composition of proper-open comparison maps
statement:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ and $v:T_2\to T_3$ be proper maps with
open immersions $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ satisfying
$u j_1=j_2$ and $v j_2=j_3$. For $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$
with finite $\Lambda$, the maps of
the comparison-map
construction satisfy

$$
\alpha_{vu,K}
= (Rv_*\alpha_{u,K})\circ\alpha_{v,K},
$$

under the canonical identification $R(vu)_*=Rv_*Ru_*$.
For the identity map the comparison is the identity.

proof.text:
We use the finite constant coefficient ring and the derived adjunction specified in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]; in particular these are etale module categories, not structure-sheaf modules or pro-etale categories. The composite $vu$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], and $(vu)j_1=j_3$, so its comparison is defined. First compute a restriction map for arbitrary $L\in D^+(T_a{}_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and a map $w:T_a\to T_b$ satisfying $wj_a=j_b$. Choose a bounded below injective representative $I$ of $L$ using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $Rw_*L$ is represented by $w_*I$, including its action on maps. Open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies open inverse image with restriction; the same identification is linear on constant-coefficient modules because [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives their underlying inverse image and action. Exactness in that proposition makes derived restriction termwise. For each etale $W\to X$ define a chain map by restriction of $I$ along
$$\delta_w(W):W\longrightarrow W\times_{T_b}T_a,\qquad z\longmapsto(z,j_a(z)).$$
Here $j_a(z)$ denotes the composite $W\to X\xrightarrow{j_a}T_a$. Both schemes are objects of $T_a{}_{\Et}$, and $\delta_w(W)$ is a morphism there. In degree $r$ this map is
$$I^r(W\times_{T_b}T_a)\longrightarrow I^r(W).$$
The scalar action is compatible with this restriction: a section of the constant ring on $W$ pulls back along $W\times_{T_b}T_a\to W$, then along $\delta_w(W)$, to itself, since their composite is $\operatorname{id}_W$. Thus the displayed maps are $\Lambda$-linear. It gives $t_{w,L}:j_b^{-1}Rw_*L\to j_a^{-1}L$. Restrictions commute with the differentials, with maps of sheaves and with chain homotopies. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], maps between injective representatives model all derived morphisms and changes of representative are homotopy equivalences. Consequently this construction is independent of the representative and natural in $L$.

proof.text:
For $w=u,v,vu$ and $L=j_{a!}K$, use the fibre product $V$, projections $b,p$ and section $s$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. The section $s$ is open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], $b^{-1}I$ is a bounded below injective representative of $b^{-1}j_{a!}K$. The restriction isomorphism $r$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] is represented by the sectionwise identity
$$ (j_b^{-1}w_*I)(W)=I(W\times_{T_b}T_a)=(p_*b^{-1}I)(W).$$
Use the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-identification]: restriction of extension by zero along the clopen section identifies $b^{-1}j_{a!}K$ with $s_!K$, and the composite of this identification, derived open restriction, and component restriction is the specified $\theta$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Thus this is a statement about the named comparison isomorphism, not merely the existence of an isomorphism between its source and $K$.
The component-restriction map of [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image] is induced by restriction along the section. On $b^{-1}I$, restriction from the object $W\times_XV$ to its distinguished component $W$ is precisely $I(\delta_w(W))$. Indeed the inclusion has projections $W\to X$ and $W\xrightarrow{j_a}T_a$, which characterize $\delta_w(W)$ by the fibre-product universal property. The restriction identification of extension by zero in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-identification] identifies the resulting complex $s^{-1}b^{-1}I=j_a^{-1}I$ with $K$. Hence, after this canonical identification of $j_a^{-1}j_{a!}K$ with $K$, the map computed in step 1 is exactly $t_{w,j_{a!}K}=\theta_{w,K}$. This calculation uses the statement that specifies the restriction composite; it does not extract an unrecorded formula for the separate base-change factor $e$ from the proof of another node. The injective terms need not vanish on the complementary component. Only the derived object is zero there, as follows from its identification with $s_!K$.

proof.text:
Compute the composition of the $t$ maps using one representative $I$ of $L\in D^+(T_1{}_{\Et},\Lambda)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], $u_*I$ is itself a bounded below complex of injectives, so it represents $Ru_*L$ and can be used to compute $Rv_*Ru_*L$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The fibre-product associator gives $(vu)_*I\cong v_*u_*I$ and is linear on constant coefficients by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. This is the canonical derived composition identification: derive this underived identification on injectives, using the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. For etale $W\to X$, the two successive restrictions are along
$$W\longrightarrow W\times_{T_2}T_1\longrightarrow (W\times_{T_3}T_2)\times_{T_2}T_1\cong W\times_{T_3}T_1.$$
The first arrow is $(\operatorname{id},j_1)$, and the second sends $(z,t_1)$ to $((z,j_2(z)),t_1)$. Under the associator their composite is $\delta_{vu}(W)$, because $uj_1=j_2$ and $vj_2=j_3$. The contravariant functoriality of each sheaf $I^r$ therefore gives, degree by degree and hence in the derived category,
$$t_{vu,L}=t_{u,L}\circ t_{v,Ru_*L}.$$
This proves the coherence used below, rather than taking it from the proof of an open-restriction node.

proof.text:
Use the derived adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Write $\eta_j:\operatorname{id}\to j^{-1}j_!$ for its unit. The open-immersion square with $g=j$, $g_U=\operatorname{id}_X$, $j'=\operatorname{id}_X$ is cartesian since $j$ is a monomorphism; [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] gives the canonical identification $j^{-1}j_!K\cong K$. Under it $\eta_{j,K}$ is the identity: the transpose formula in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] sends each local section of $K$ to that same section on every etale object factoring through $X$, and the derived adjunction uses the same unit termwise. Thus the defining adjoint property of $\alpha$ is exactly
$$j_b^{-1}\alpha_{w,K}=\theta_{w,K}^{-1}.$$
Equality of maps out of $j_{b!}K$ is detected by these restricted maps, because their transposes are $j_b^{-1}(-)\circ\eta_{j_b,K}$ and the adjunction is a bijection.

proof.text:
Set $A=j_{1!}K$ and $\beta=(Rv_*\alpha_{u,K})\circ\alpha_{v,K}$. Naturality of $t_v$, applied to $\alpha_{u,K}:j_{2!}K\to Ru_*A$, gives
$$t_{v,Ru_*A}\circ j_3^{-1}(Rv_*\alpha_{u,K})=(j_2^{-1}\alpha_{u,K})\circ t_{v,j_{2!}K}.$$
Using the composition calculation of step 3, the identification of step 2 and the defining transpose equation of step 4, one obtains
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta_{vu,K}\circ j_3^{-1}\beta
&=\theta_{u,K}\circ t_{v,Ru_*A}\circ j_3^{-1}(Rv_*\alpha_{u,K})\circ j_3^{-1}\alpha_{v,K}\\
&=\theta_{u,K}\circ(j_2^{-1}\alpha_{u,K})\circ\theta_{v,K}\circ j_3^{-1}\alpha_{v,K}\\
&=\operatorname{id}_K.
\end{aligned}$$
The same equation holds for $\alpha_{vu,K}$ by its definition [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Since $\theta_{vu,K}$ is invertible, the two restricted maps agree. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection from step 4 proves $\beta=\alpha_{vu,K}$, with the canonical derived composition identification computed in step 3.

proof.text: For $w=\operatorname{id}_{T}$ and $j_a=j_b=j$, the map $\delta_w(W):W\to W\times_TT$ is the canonical identity fibre-product identification. Hence the section formula in step 1 makes $t_{w,L}$ the identity after $R(\operatorname{id}_T)_*\cong\operatorname{id}$. By step 2 its value on $j_!K$ is the specified $\theta_{w,K}=\operatorname{id}_K$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] now says that $\alpha_{w,K}$ and $\operatorname{id}_{j_!K}$ have the same transpose, namely the unit $K\to j^{-1}j_!K$, identified with $\operatorname{id}_K$ in step 4. The adjunction bijection gives the identity assertion.
